title.text: Recognize impairment without a safe-drink inference

why_how.text: Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.
The handbook describes alcohol moving from the stomach and small intestine into the blood and throughout the body.
Food in the stomach slows the described absorption compared with an empty stomach; it does not establish safe driving after drinking.
Alcohol can dull judgment, inhibition and self-control and impair reaction, coordination, balance, vision and distance judgment.
Once alcohol is in the blood, aspirin, coffee, breathing exercises, a slap, physical exercise or food do not sober a person; the source identifies time as the recovery factor.
Alcohol can change mood and create false confidence while slowing thinking and reaction.
The handbook lists excessive speed, weaving, unusually slow travel, jerky controls and abrupt stops as possible signs of an impaired driver.

scenario.text: A learner faces this decision: Can a person safely rely on personal or friends’ judgments of driving ability after drinking?

reasoning.text: The proposed response is “Yes, if friends say the person looks normal”. That alternative does not preserve the stated rule. Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.

result.text: Choose “No; impairment can occur before visible signs”. Keep the setting and every stated condition attached to that response.

claim.text: Common mistake: “Yes, if friends say the person looks normal”.

correction.text: Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.

memory_support.text: Remember “Recognize impairment without a safe drink”. Connect the person or setting to the required action, then check the full statement for limits or exceptions.

prompt.text: Consider the earlier decision. Is “Yes, if friends say the person looks normal” a sound response? Give the correction and explain the condition that decides it.

answer.text: Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.

rationale.text: The correction follows the stated rule rather than the proposed alternative. Do not rely on personal or friends' judgments of driving ability after drinking; impairment can occur before visible signs appear.

why_how.text: The source's open-container summary prohibits both the driver and passengers from drinking alcohol or possessing an open alcoholic-beverage container in a vehicle.
For the described transport of unsealed alcohol, the handbook directs using the trunk or, if there is no trunk, a position behind the rearmost upright seat.
Avoid driving while affected by a drug that could interfere with safe vehicle operation.
Combining alcohol with certain medications or drugs can increase impairment and interfere with driving tasks.
Ask the prescribing clinician whether a medicine causes drowsiness or otherwise affects driving; if it does, arrange another driver while taking it.
Read nonprescription medicine labels and do not drive when the instructions discourage it.
The handbook describes drug-impaired driving as being under the influence of either legal or illegal substances.
The source describes marijuana as slowing reactions and impairing time and distance judgment.
The source associates methamphetamine and cocaine with aggressive or reckless behavior.
The source describes opioids as causing drowsiness and affecting memory or thinking, and sedatives as causing dizziness or drowsiness.

title.text: Plan transport and retain BAC conditions

why_how.text: Impairment-prevention strategies include choosing a designated driver, having that driver keep the keys and arranging rides to and from gatherings involving alcohol or drugs.
Other source prevention strategies are avoiding drug-and-alcohol parties and discussing impaired-driving risks with friends.
The handbook's under-twenty-one DUI BAC threshold is zero point zero two or higher.
For the noncommercial driver aged twenty-one or older, the handbook's DUI BAC threshold is zero point zero eight or higher.
The source states that a concentration of zero point twenty or more carries increased penalties.
A BAC below zero point zero eight does not preclude a DUI conviction involving other intoxicating substances.

scenario.text: A learner faces this decision: Which strategy matches the handbook’s impairment-prevention guidance?

reasoning.text: The proposed response is “Wait for visible impairment before planning a ride”. That alternative does not preserve the stated rule. Impairment-prevention strategies include choosing a designated driver, having that driver keep the keys and arranging rides to and from gatherings involving alcohol or drugs.

result.text: Choose “Choose a designated driver who keeps the keys and arrange rides to and from gatherings”. Keep the setting and every stated condition attached to that response.

correction.text: Impairment-prevention strategies include choosing a designated driver, having that driver keep the keys and arranging rides to and from gatherings involving alcohol or drugs.

title.text: Distinguish insurance proof and conditional sanctions

why_how.text: The source identifies an SR-twenty-two as an insurer's certified statement of liability coverage used as proof of financial responsibility.
The handbook requires one year of financial-responsibility proof for a first violation of Idaho's no-insurance law.
For a second no-insurance offense within five years, the source requires financial-responsibility proof for three years.
The general adult first-DUI-conviction list gives up to six months in jail and a fine up to one thousand dollars.
That general adult first-conviction list gives a mandatory suspension from ninety through one hundred eighty days, with no driving in its first thirty days.
For a second adult conviction within ten years, the general list gives mandatory jail from ten days through one year and a fine up to two thousand dollars.
The general adult second-conviction list requires a one-year license suspension when the second conviction is within ten years.
For an adult's third or later conviction within ten years, the general list gives mandatory jail from thirty days to ten years and a fine up to five thousand dollars.
The same adult third-or-later conviction carries the source's mandatory one-through-five-year suspension and felony classification.
The printed under-twenty-one suspension parentheticals give one year for a first conviction and two years for a second within ten years.
For an under-twenty-one third or later conviction within ten years, the printed suspension is one year or until age twenty-one, whichever is longer.

reasoning.text: The proposed response is “A permission to drive without liability coverage”. That alternative does not preserve the stated rule. The source identifies an SR-twenty-two as an insurer's certified statement of liability coverage used as proof of financial responsibility.

result.text: Choose “An insurer’s certified liability-coverage statement used as financial-responsibility proof”. Keep the setting and every stated condition attached to that response.

correction.text: The source identifies an SR-twenty-two as an insurer's certified statement of liability coverage used as proof of financial responsibility.

why_how.text: During a traffic stop, remain calm, signal and pull off or aside as soon as safely possible.
After stopping for an officer, switch off the engine and radio, remain inside unless told to exit and keep the hands visible on the steering wheel.
The traffic-stop guidance says neither the driver nor passengers should use phones or mobile devices during the encounter.
Tell the officer at first contact if a weapon is in the vehicle.
An officer may request the license, insurance proof and registration; if they are out of reach, explain their location before reaching.
If directed to leave the vehicle, remain clear of traffic and keep hands plainly visible.
An officer may conclude a stop with a warning or ticket; a ticket can include a fine and may be contested in court.
The source says signing and accepting a traffic ticket does not admit guilt, while refusing to sign may lead to arrest.
Report perceived officer misconduct promptly to the agency; the ticket lists identifying information, which may also be requested from the officer.
